quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the road becomes slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: When driving in rain, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In rain, use your low beam headlights to see the road better.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic is coming from both directions.
An extra lane is being added.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is coming from both directions.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that traffic may be coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: Keeping space between your vehicle and other vehicles is important because it:

options.text: Gives you time to react to surprises.
Keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react to surprises.
questions.explanation: Leaving plenty of space between you and other vehicles gives you time to react if other drivers make mistakes.

questions.question: ____ can limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level above the legal limit
Even a small amount of alcohol
Only a blood alcohol level above 0.05 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: Even a small amount of alcohol
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. No one can drink and drive safely.

questions.question: If you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get away from it.
Stop right away and block its path.
Do everything you can to clear the way for it.
Signal to it when it is safe to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do everything you can to clear the way for it.
questions.explanation: You must clear the way for emergency vehicles. Pull to the side of the road and stop if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, you must:

options.text: Drive to the right side and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: Yield to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. Drive to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, pass through it first before stopping on the right side.

questions.question: When approaching an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop only if you are involved or emergency help hasn't arrived.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help hasn't arrived. Stay focused on driving and keep moving. Do not stop just to look.

questions.question: An "End school zone" sign means:

options.text: A reduced speed zone is starting.
The reduced speed zone is ending.

questions.correctAnswerText: The reduced speed zone is ending.
questions.explanation: Follow the school zone speed limit during the posted times. This sign marks the end of the reduced speed area.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your:
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, along with fog lights if your vehicle has them. High beams bounce off fog and reduce visibility.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Open your door to check if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window while backing. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate.
One driver should proceed without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles should go in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must let the vehicle on the right go first.

questions.question: On a two-lane road without bike lanes, how should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Slow down and wait for oncoming traffic to clear. Then pass while giving the bicyclist plenty of space.
Keep driving straight. The bicyclist should move out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
Honk to let the bicyclist know you are about to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for oncoming traffic to clear. Then pass while giving the bicyclist plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicycle like you would pass any other vehicle, but not too fast or close. Leave at least 3 feet of space between your mirror and the bicyclist, or 5 feet on faster roads or when there are multiple bicyclists. Honking can startle riders and cause crashes.

questions.question: When doing a zipper merge near a construction zone, what should drivers do?

options.text: Stay in your lane until the merge point.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane until the merge point.
questions.explanation: When you see a 'Lane closed ahead' sign, stay in your lane until the merge point. Then take turns with other drivers to merge safely and smoothly into the open lane.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, what happens?

options.text: Your body breaks it down faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your reactions slow down.
questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, it slows your reactions, makes you feel more confident, and causes you to make more mistakes.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?

options.text: Remove your foot from the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove your foot from the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: On a slippery road, first take your foot off the gas pedal. If you need to slow down more, gently press the brake pedal with steady, light pressure.

questions.question: You are in a line of vehicles at a stop sign. If there is no oncoming traffic after the cars ahead pass through, what must you do?

options.text: You can go through without stopping again.
You must stop at the stop sign or stop line before going.
You can slowly roll past the stop sign.
You can follow the car ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at the stop sign or stop line before going.
questions.explanation: You must always come to a complete stop at a stop sign and check for traffic before proceeding. Do not feel rushed by other cars to skip making a complete stop.

questions.question: What do orange colored signs mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone signs
questions.explanation: Work zones on highways use orange signs shaped like diamonds with black letters or symbols. These signs warn that people are working on or near the highway.

questions.question: Which of these must you obey before the others?
questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions take priority over all traffic signs, signals, and road markings. Traffic officers, police, fire police, road workers, and school crossing guards are all authorized to direct traffic.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs tell you?

options.text: The possible speeds for the area
The highest or lowest speed you are legally allowed to drive
The speed to drive in heavy traffic
The speed to drive in poor conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest speed you are legally allowed to drive
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest or lowest safe speed allowed on a road. The maximum limits are for ideal conditions. You must slow down when conditions require it.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal to ask the driver to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they are crossing against a red light or crossing in an unsafe way.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs mean you must stop and check for traffic. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about driving on a wet roadway?

options.text: When you drive faster, your tires grip the road less.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
When you slow down, the roadway becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you drive faster, your tires grip the road less.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on a wet road, the less your tires grip the pavement. If you go too fast, your tires can lose contact with the road and you will hydroplane, or slide on a layer of water.

questions.question: Large vehicles have blind spots that can extend up to 200 feet directly behind the vehicle.
questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have blind spots up to 200 feet behind them. Do not follow closely behind large vehicles because the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: When using a roundabout, drivers should:

options.text: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: In a roundabout, you must enter from the right and yield to cars already in the circle. Follow the circle counterclockwise until you reach your road.

questions.question: When you see this black and yellow sign, it means:

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right due to roadwork.
Slow down because the road ahead curves sharply in this direction.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road ahead curves sharply in this direction.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the road ahead will make a sharp curve. Slow down before the curve, just as you would at an intersection.

questions.question: You have the right-of-way when turning left on which of the following traffic signals?
questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in the direction the arrow points. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.
questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: To prepare for anything coming up on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Continually scan the entire road and roadsides.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus only on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continually scan the entire road and roadsides.
questions.explanation: Look far ahead and scan the entire road and sides. Do not just stare at the center. Finding problems early helps you avoid danger.

questions.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle has the speed needed to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe passing requires three things: clear visibility ahead, enough space to return to your lane before oncoming traffic, and a vehicle capable of passing speed. Only pass where it is legal and safe.

questions.question: You may not park:

options.text: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When you park on the street, you must stay within 12 inches of the edge of the road.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is a driver who:

options.text: Looks at things off the road or daydreams while driving.
Makes eye contact with a passenger while driving.
Only watches the car directly ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by looking at passengers, searching in your car, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming. Keep scanning the road, check your mirrors, and look at your dashboard regularly. Good habits like these help you stay focused while driving.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while you are driving. You should:

options.text: Grip the steering wheel tightly and slow down gradually.
Turn on your emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the steering wheel tightly and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not hit the brakes right away. Hold the steering wheel firmly to stay in your lane. Let off the gas and slow down gradually. When you are going very slowly, gently apply the brakes and pull safely off the road.

questions.question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle, you must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: If you are driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Let the motorcycle use only half a lane.
Share the same lane when passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle has the same rights as any other vehicle on the road. Give motorcyclists a full lane width. Even if a lane looks big enough for two vehicles, a motorcycle needs room to move safely.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use your high beam headlights.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn drivers you are entering.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert others.
Drive out fast to merge smoothly with traffic.
Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must give the right-of-way to pedestrians and vehicles on the roadway.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you must slow down, give them the right-of-way, and proceed with caution. Be ready to stop to protect the pedestrian.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity.
questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the harder your vehicle hits if you crash.

questions.question: You need extra caution near a pedestrian with a white cane because:

options.text: He or she is a police officer.
He or she has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: He or she is blind.
questions.explanation: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you must slow down, give them the right-of-way, and proceed with caution. Be ready to stop to protect the pedestrian.
